Subject: Residency & retention clarifications for Redwood hosted API

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo last week — Shoreline's engineering and compliance teams had a couple of follow-ups related to data residency and deletion for the hosted API before we can move ahead with the trial. Can you confirm the following?

1) Where customer prompt/response data is stored by default (region-level) and whether we can request EU-only storage for Shoreline data.
2) What the default retention period is for non-PII telemetry and request logs, and whether retention can be shortened via contract.
3) For deletion requests: what the end-to-end timeline is (acknowledgement, queueing, physical deletion from backups) and whether you provide attestation when deletion completes.

We typically need evidence we can share with our auditors (SaaS vendor checklist). If you have a one-pager or runbook that spells this out, that would help.

Appreciate a short-answer summary and any attachments.

Best,
Claire
Claire D'Souza
Head of IT Compliance
Shoreline Health

Subject: Re: Residency & retention clarifications for Redwood hosted API

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Irene has the technical runbook and I've looped Ben (Sales) for contract/term questions. I'll attach our short evidence packet.

1) Storage regions: By default, hosted API data is stored in the region nearest the customer account (we advertise region-aware hosting). For Shoreline we can provision EU-only tenancy (Ireland or Frankfurt) prior to trial start; that is a standard setup step.

2) Default retention: request logs and non-PII telemetry are retained for 90 days by default. We support contract-specified retention windows down to 30 days for hosted customers on our standard SLAs.

3) Deletion workflow and attestation: Deletion requests are acknowledged within 24 hours, queued and processed within our deletion pipeline (typical completion 3–7 business days for primary data). Backups are retained with immutable snapshots for up to 30 days beyond primary deletion; we run a purge job that removes eligible snapshots on a 30-day cadence. We provide a deletion attestation PDF (signed) upon request for enterprise customers.

See attached: hostedapi-data-flow.pdf (diagram), deletion-playbook.pdf (runbook + attestation template).

If you want, Irene can reply with more detail on caching (KV/prefix) behavior and exact RPCs we run during an erasure.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Markus — that's helpful. A couple of quick clarifications from the legal team:

We may need an aggressive deletion SLA in the contract if we proceed (legal will propose language). Can you or Irene confirm whether accelerated purge (7-day) is operationally feasible and what the limitations are?

Thanks — Claire

Hi Claire,

Thanks — wanted to provide the operational detail you asked for and call out constraints so legal has accurate expectations. Short answers first, then the mechanics:

Short answers
• Accelerated purge: Yes, we can support a contracted accelerated purge SLA for specific datasets (target window: 7 business days). This requires a dedicated purge ticket and legal approval; we also recommend a canary deletion in staging before production purge to validate non-targeted data isn't impacted.
• Attestation token: Our deletion attestation includes a unique audit token (UUID) and references to the internal purge ticket (REDW-XXXX). Auditors can map that token to an immutable deletion event in our audit log export.

Operational details
• Primary data deletion: We run a three-stage erasure pipeline — (1) mark and quarantine: metadata flags the dataset as subject to deletion and removes routing from active caches, (2) logical erase: application-layer records and object pointers are removed/overwritten, and (3) verification: background job confirms object unlinking and returns a verification digest. Typical primary deletion finishes within the 7 business day accelerated SLA (3–7 business days in practice).
• Cache & KV stores: We actively evict model KV caches and prefix caches for the customer tenant as part of the mark-and-quarantine step; these are in-memory or ephemeral on GPUs and cleared immediately as part of the request.
• Backups & snapshots: Backups are on a 30-day rolling retention by default. For accelerated purge, we add a targeted purge job that removes snapshots containing the customer's objects; depending on snapshot granularity this may require reconstructing snapshot manifests to identify affected blobs — this adds operational overhead and is why 7 business days is our contracted target rather than a 24–48 hour guarantee.
• Evidence & attestation: After verification we generate a deletion attestation PDF containing: customer name, dataset identifiers, deletion date range, audit token (UUID), and reference to the internal ticket. We can also provide an export of the relevant audit log entries (redacted where required).

Limitations & notes
• Cross-region copies: If data was replicated to a different region prior to request, purge runs against all replicas but timing may vary due to inter-region transfer windows — contract should specify region-scoped obligations if that is a concern.
• Immutable legal holds: If Shoreline requires legal holds for specific datasets, deletion will be paused until hold release; we support legal-hold tagging with admin controls.

Next steps
If you'd like, Ben can coordinate the contract language for a 7-day accelerated purge addendum and we'll include the attestation template in the SOW. I can also provide the audit log sample export (scrubbed) for your auditors to validate mapping.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
